topic: Living Things Grow, Respond, and Reproduce
key_concepts: Living things grow, respond to their surroundings, and reproduce.
Nonliving things do not grow, respond, or reproduce.
Seeds germinate and seedlings grow larger over time.
Young animals grow bigger and their body parts change as they become adults.
Plants respond to light by growing toward it.
Plant shoots grow upward against the direction of gravity.
Some plants respond to touch by curling or clinging.
Animals use senses and body parts to respond to food or danger.
Plants can reproduce by seeds or by planting parts such as stems, roots, and leaves.
Animals reproduce by laying eggs or by giving birth.
Living things have life cycles from young to adult.
Reproduction helps plant and animal populations continue.
